newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sees new Gatorade adding sales.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sees new Gatorade adding sales.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Thursday it expects its new "Frost" line could add $100 million in sales for its $1.4 billion Gatorade sports drink, its largest brand.
"I think (net sales for Frost) are in the range of a $100 million opportunity, net of cannibalization," James Doyle, Quaker's executive vice president of worldwide beverages, told a press conference.
Before accounting for cannibalization--the sales that are drawn away from Gatorade's existing line--total Frost sales likely will be above that $100 million target, Doyle said.
As previously reported, Quaker is rolling out the Frost line in the United States with three flavors.
The Frost line has the same formulation as traditional Gatorade, but the flavors have a "cooling" taste, Doyle said.
New products such as the Frost line will continue to be a thrust for Gatorade, which accounts for a large portion of the company's total sales of over $5.0 billion.
Doyle said more than 40 percent of Gatorade's 1996 sales came from packaging or flavors introduced in the last three years.
In foods, which includes oatmeal, cold cereals, and pasta and rice dishes, Quaker said its goal for 1997 is to achieve sales growth in the four to six percent range.
The company said it sees opportunities to grow its branded cereal business, with innovations in its long-time Life and Cap'n Crunch brands, and its expanding bagged cereal line.
